title: The use of XLSTAT in conducting principal component analysis (PCA) when evaluating the relationships between sensory and quality attributes in grilled foods
author: Vidal, Manful, et al.
materials: Step1: Start XLSTAT command to commence using XLSTAT
Step2: Select Analyzing data/ Principal components analysis command

steps.title: Launch XLSTAT
steps.instruction: Start the XLSTAT command to commence using XLSTAT.

steps.title: Open PCA module
steps.instruction: Select the “Analyzing data → Principal components analysis” command.

steps.title: Select data range
steps.instruction: Highlight the data on the Excel sheet in the Principal component dialog box; choose the data format “observations/variables” and set the PCA standardization to Pearson's correlation.

steps.title: Standardize data
steps.instruction: In the Options tab, activate “n” standardization to standardize the data.

steps.title: Add supplementary variables
steps.instruction: In the Supplementary data tab, activate “Supplementary variables” and “Quantitative” boxes, then select the consumer sensory attribute scores as supplementary quantitative variables (these do not affect distance calculations but aid interpretation).

steps.title: Handle missing data
steps.instruction: In the Data options tab, choose “Do not accept missing data”.

substeps.instruction: Descriptive statistics to obtain a summary table of the data set.
Bartlett's sphericity test (α = 0.05) to test if the correlation matrix is an identity matrix.
Kaiser‑Meyer‑Olkin test to assess suitability for factor analysis.

steps.title: Set variable charts
steps.instruction: In the Charts tab → Variables sub‑tab, check the boxes for Correlations charts and Vectors.

steps.title: Set observation charts
steps.instruction: In the Charts → Observations sub‑tab, check Observation charts, Colored labels, and Color by group to display observations with group‑based colors.

steps.title: Configure biplots
steps.instruction: In the Charts → Biplots sub‑tab, check Biplots; under Options for variables, enable Vectors and Labels; under Options for observations, enable Labels; set Type of biplot to “Distance biplot” and Coefficient to “Automatic”.

steps.title: Disable bootstrap chart
steps.instruction: In the Charts → Bootstrap charts sub‑tab, uncheck the Bootstrap observations chart option, then click OK to start PCA computations.

steps.title: Display results
steps.instruction: Select the principal component(s) to plot (the first two factors explain 90.47% of total variation for this data set) and click Done to output the PCA results.
